properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (third pass): user-flagged overlap between HDY3/HDY1-2 and between E2/H1 and E3/H2 -- both were transcription errors (HDY1/2's diagonal notch was oversimplified into a plain rectangle that re-overlapped HDY3; E2/E3's bottom edge was misread as the row further south, landing on top of H1/H2). Re-read against the diagram's own gridlines and confirmed zero geometric overlap with the adjacent block this time. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a full-site overlay check (every Pier 70 approximate polygon drawn directly on Figure 3.3.1/6.4.2) found this block's traced shape was both too narrow (its east edge stopped ~150m short of Parcel C2's real west edge, when the diagram shows them sharing a border) and encroached upward into the Irish Hill Remnant open-space area to its north -- a real corner-misread, not the third-pass notch bug. Re-measured this block's true quadrilateral directly from Figure 6.4.2's own colored fill (isolating this legend color) with a fresh grid-overlay crop: pixel corners NW(423,1125), NE(985,1125), SE(985,1230), SW(225,1230) -- NE/SE now share an exact boundary with Parcel C2's own already-committed west edge (x~985), and the NW-SW diagonal now matches the real cut separating this block from the Irish Hill Remnant park to its north, rather than cutting into it. Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. This 4-corner box created a small (357 m2) new overlap with HDY3's own south point -- clipped against HDY3's current geometry via shapely difference() (the two are adjacent planned parcels that should meet cleanly, unlike the Building 2 case below) to close it, producing the 6-vertex shape now in this file. Also creates a small (~400 m2) new overlap with 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' along this block's east edge -- left un-clipped, same reasoning as Building 2's own file: both are approximate placeholders competing for the same currently-undivided vacant lot, and clipping either would not make either more accurate. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (second pass, same day): user-flagged visual check found the same-day fix above was itself wrong -- it assumed this block's east edge touches Parcel C2's west edge, but Figure 6.4.2 actually shows a real gap (part of the Irish Hill Playground open space) between them, roughly 40-45px/~35m wide. Re-measured this block's ENTIRE shape programmatically instead of patching corners: isolated this legend color (RGB [169,143,173]) in a fresh crop, connected-component labeled it separately from HDY3 (they don't touch in the raster, confirming they're genuinely separate), and extracted its precise contour (OpenCV, simplified to its 4 real corners, dropping the small zigzags caused by this block's own internal dashed sub-division lines). Result: NW(561,1124), NE(923,1124), SE(923,1246), and a point where the diagonal cut meets 22nd St (464,1238) in pixel space -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. This replaces both of today's earlier patches; confirmed zero overlap with HDY3 and with Parcel C2 (a real, unclaimed gap remains between this block and C2, matching the diagram). RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (same day, full geometry restart): the small ~400 m2 overlap this file previously noted with 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' no longer applies -- that file's placement was corrected to its real east-cluster position next to Buildings 12 and 21 (see that file's digitization_method); this block no longer overlaps it. EXEMPTED FROM STREET CLIPPING 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'HDY1/2 is split in 2 and I don't understand why'): Michigan St's real centerline (CNN 8999000, a single ~2,800m-long official segment) runs continuously from 20th St all the way down through this block's own interior to 22nd St. Its northern portion is confirmed real, built pavement (visually verified near Building 14/Building 2 earlier this project). At THIS block's latitude, satellite imagery shows no clear curb or paving -- a pixel-color pavement check came back ambiguous (60%, neither a clean confirm nor a clean reject) and a direct look shows what might be a worn, informal site-access track through an active equipment-staging area, not a real, curbed city street. Regardless of whether some access track exists today, Figure 6.4.2 draws this block as ONE undivided parcel with no street through it -- the same 'map the plan, not today's ad hoc site conditions' principle already established for PKN/PKS. Rather than truncate Michigan St's real, legitimately-long official segment (which would break its correct use further north), exempted this block itself from street clipping so it renders as the single block the diagram shows, instead of being silently cut into two disconnected pieces by a real street's centerline passing through informally-used land this parcel is planned to consolidate. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (found by src/verify_block_fill.py, a new reusable diagram-fit checker built after user feedback that too much of this project's QA was one-off pixel investigation that's easy to get subtly wrong and hard to redo consistently): this block was never rechecked for the 2376x1836-vs-2200x1700 resolution-mismatch bug independently found and fixed on PKN/PKS/HDY3/C1/Building 21 on 2026-09-17 -- it slipped through because that day's fixes were driven by individual user-flagged visual checks, not a systematic re-verification of every block. The tool flagged this block's committed geometry at only 0.11 IoU against a fresh color-fill re-extraction. Confirmed: this block's own pixel corners (561,1124)-(923,1124)-(923,1246)-(464,1238), unchanged since the 2026-09-16 second pass, were recorded from the 2376x1836 source and never rescaled. Divided by 1.08 and reconverted via the same validated 6-point affine transform: (519.4,1040.7)-(854.6,1040.7)-(854.6,1153.7)-(429.6,1146.3), closely matching a fresh, independent re-extraction on page171.png. Area changes from ~4,682 to ~4,015 sq m. Re-verified 0 overlap with HDY3 (13.9m gap, similar to before) and Irish Hill Playground (0.9m gap, effectively touching, slightly improved); 12% real-street overlap (was not previously checked at this corrected position), under this project's MAJOR_CLIP threshold. EXTENDED 2026-09-17 (same day/pass as HDY3's own 22nd-St extension, prompted by the same user instruction): re-examined Figure 6.4.2 directly and confirmed this block's own south edge IS drawn sitting right on the '22ND ST' boundary line in the diagram -- the ~40m gap this block's own (already-corrected, IoU-verified) position had to the REAL 22nd St curb was a real-vs-diagram discrepancy, the same general phenomenon already documented for the '21st St (NEW)' row, not a tracing error in this block's own diagram-fit (which independently re-verified at IoU 0.96 earlier the same day). Extended this block's two southern corners (SE, SW) straight down to the real 22nd St curb line (6.8m north of centerline) at their own longitudes, preserving the NW/NE corners and the block's own diagonal-cut shape otherwise. Area grows from ~4,015 to ~9,146 sq m as a direct, expected consequence of reaching the real curb rather than stopping ~40m short of it. ADJUSTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: this block's south edge, set exactly at the 6.8m real curb line, eats into the sidewalk): moved the south edge (SE/SW) out to 9.8m north of the real 22nd St centerline instead of 6.8m -- adding a ~3m sidewalk allowance beyond the bare curb, consistent with the D4D's own cited 55-67ft ROW range for this class of street (implying more room behind the curb than the curb measurement alone accounts for). Area shrinks slightly from the previous (curb-only) version. NARROWED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: resolve the HDY3/HDY1-2 diagonal disconnect): the prior round found no real room for a separate Irish Hill corridor between this block's west corner and Illinois St's real right-of-way (2-9m at most). Per user instruction to resolve rather than accept the direct-touching compromise, moved this block's own west corner (v4) east by ~12m (from -122.38722 to -122.3871), trading a modest amount of this block's own area for a real, meaningful gap to HDY3 (see that file). Area drops from ~9,146 to ~8,447 sq m. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged, second time: 'HDY1/2 and C2 still eat away at the sidewalk on the south side' and separately 'the diagonal you create... should be made of 2 parallel edges'): (1) this block's own SW corner (v3) was found ~0.8m short of the intended 9.8m real-22nd-St-centerline offset (a small residual from an earlier, less precise calculation) -- recomputed precisely (lat 37.758093552044336 -> 37.758100765844276); its SE corner (v2), independently checked the same way, was already exactly correct and is unchanged. (2) this corner (v3) is also one endpoint of the diagonal corridor edge (v3-v0) facing HDY3's own corresponding edge -- that pair was flagged as visibly non-parallel (11.2 degrees here vs 19.1 degrees on HDY3's side). Kept this block's own v3-v0 edge exactly as-is (bearing 11.2 degrees) as the reference, and rotated HDY3's corresponding edge to match it instead -- see pier70_hdy3.geojson's digitization_method for the full writeup; confirmed the two edges are now a uniform ~17.0m apart along their whole length (genuinely parallel) rather than converging/diverging as before. REBUILT 2026-09-17 (user-flagged, third time: 'HYD3 is too messed up' -- sent an unlabeled version of the map and hand-drew a replacement for both HDY3 and this block): the formula-driven fix above was rejected on sight; user drew directly on out/pier70_unlabeled.png and asked for it to be used as the baseline. Digitized via ORB feature matching (crop-to-full-render registration, 393/419 inlier keypoints) plus an independent marker-based pixel<->lon/lat calibration of the full render (sub-pixel residuals) -- see pier70_hdy3.geojson's own digitization_method for the full pipeline writeup, which covers both files together. This block's own east edge (NE, SE corners) came back within 1-3m of its already-committed position, confirming the user's sketch traces the EXISTING east edge rather than redesigning it -- kept those two corners exactly as before, unchanged. The two corners that DO change are the ones the user's message called out directly: (1) the corridor-top corner (formerly 'v0' at -122.38692933990407,37.75877958601038) moved to the user's drawn position, ~50m east and ~7m south of the old one -- this also seeds the new, wider corridor gap to HDY3. (2) the south corner facing 22nd St (formerly 'v3') moved to the user's drawn position, explicitly pulled north of the real curb+9.8m-offset line this project had been using -- per the user's own annotation ('notice how I excluded the south sidewalk'), this hand-verified position is now authoritative for this corner rather than the formulaic curb offset, since the user is looking at the same satellite basemap this map is built on and judging the visible sidewalk directly. Area shrinks from ~8,406 to ~6,446 sq m as a direct result of both pulled-in corners. Re-verified: 0 overlap with C2 (0.1m gap) and with HDY3 (17m parallel corridor gap, see that file); this block keeps its street_clip_exempt flag and its own real-street-buffer overlap (~14%) is expected/unflagged under that exemption, same as before. ADJUSTED 2026-09-17 (two more user-flagged issues, same message): (1) 'HDY1/2 and C2 south border should align with sidewalk south side' -- direct satellite comparison (src/satellite_check.py, reference lines drawn at 6.8m/9.8m/13m/18.8m offsets from the real 22nd St centerline across the WHOLE Illinois-to-Louisiana frontage) showed the user's own hand-drawn v3 corner (west end) sits at exactly 18.8m off the centerline, not the 9.8m this project had been using -- and that 18.8m reading matches the real sidewalk/lot boundary visible in the imagery much better than 9.8m did at this corner. Applied that same, higher-confidence 18.8m offset to this block's other south corner (v2, east end, near C2) instead of the old 9.8m, so this block's whole south edge reflects one consistently-verified sidewalk clearance rather than mixing a hand-verified value with an older formula value. (2) 'HDY1/2 north edge should be parallel to C1 south (and north) edge' -- this block's own v0 (corridor-top/north corner) previously sat on a line through v3 matching HDY3's own corridor bearing only; the v0-v1 edge (this block's actual north-facing edge, toward C1/Irish Hill Playground) was not parallel to C1's own south edge (86.5 degrees) at all. Recomputed v0 as the intersection of two lines: one through v1 at C1's exact south-edge bearing (86.5 degrees), and one through v3 at HDY3's own corridor-edge bearing (35.2 degrees, unchanged) -- satisfying both parallelism requirements at once with v1 and v3 held fixed. New v0 is ~10m east and ~14m north of the old one. Re-verified: polygon still simple/valid; re-triggered a matching re-clip of Irish Hill Playground (see that file) since it shares this corner.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. CORRECTED 2026-09-17: fixed a resolution-mismatch bug that had gone unnoticed since 2026-09-16 -- see digitization_method.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential per Brookfield's leasing brochure, 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2. Shown as one combined parcel (HDY1/2) distinct from HDY3 in the D4D's own figure -- not three separately-numbered HDY1/HDY2/HDY3 parcels as sometimes described secondhand. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
